title: Noise lower bound for low-degree energy
statement:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, and let $p$ be a real coefficient family on the subsets of $[n]$ that vanishes on every subset of size greater than $k$. For $0\le\rho\le1$, the noise operator applied to the Boolean-cube function represented by $p$ satisfies
\[
\rho^{2k}\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}p(S)^2\le \mathbb E\!\left[(T_\rho P_p)^2\right],
\]
where the expectation is uniform on the cube.
hypotheses_covered: p has degree at most k
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients; degree at most $k$ means $a_S=0$ for $|S|>k$. If $P$ has degree at most the integer $k\ge0$ and $0\le\rho\le1$, define $T_\rho P=\sum_S\rho^{|S|}a_S\chi_S$. Then $\rho^{2k}\sum_Sa_S^2\le\mathbb E[(T_\rho P)^2]$, with natural powers including $0^0=1$.
